nieuw.titel: Keep skirmishers outside a ranked pursuer's arc
nieuw.tekst: Use skirmishers' movement in any direction to keep escaping a ranked unit's charge arc. Let the pursuit waste its time while preserving your skirmishers' points.
nieuw.waarom: He says ranked units can spend several turns approaching only for the skirmishers to march out of their arc again. In his view, the time gained can also expose the pursuer to a hammer attacking from the side.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He describes games where enemy units spent three turns marching towards him, after which he simply marched back outside their arc.

extraCitaten.citaat: going to preserve their points, which is what wins in the game.

nieuw.waarom: He says a skirmishing screen can provide hard cover to the unit behind it, making that unit difficult to hit.

nieuw.titel: Equip a mounted hunter with protection and a magic weapon
nieuw.tekst: He recommends a mounted hero with movement in all directions, a magic weapon and the Icon of Fortitude to chase skirmishers. He suggests getting its armour save to 2+.
nieuw.waarom: He values the Icon of Fortitude because it prevents the character being killed by a single cannon shot.

nieuw.titel: Offset the front skirmisher to protect against overruns
nieuw.tekst: Place the front skirmisher to one side of the unit you want to protect, while the remaining models continue screening it. Use that front model to choose where the enemy charge makes contact.
nieuw.waarom: He says the charger must reach the front model, letting you set the point of contact even though the skirmishers align to the charger.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He warns that you must predict where the unit will form up and maintain coherency so models do not die trying to reach the back rank.

bronnen.citaat: you can set the point where the charge takes place.

extraCitaten.citaat: maximum coherency so you don't lose models

nieuw.titel: Rear-charge with skirmishers to add combat resolution
nieuw.tekst: Use mobile skirmishers to charge the rear of an enemy already fighting your strong unit in front. Value the extra two combat resolution even when you do not expect the skirmishers to cause damage.
nieuw.waarom: He says rolling to hit, wound and penetrate saves often produces few wounds, so an extra two combat resolution is substantial.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He says the skirmishers cannot disrupt the enemy's rank bonus this way.

bronnen.citaat: they're providing plus two by just hitting into the back

extraCitaten.citaat: but you can often add to the combat in the front

nieuw.waarom: He says the heavy unit lacks mobility and wants to stay central. The skirmishers' position behind the enemy also gives them a head start when pursuing.

nieuw.waarom: He says the skirmishers' superior mobility lets them escape ranked pursuers.
